title: Japanese uses three writing systems at once

publish.title: Japanese uses three writing systems at once
publish.description: Hiragana, katakana and kanji, and what each is for.

scenes.headline: Three writing systems at once
scenes.narration: A single Japanese sentence can use three different scripts. Here is what each one does.

scenes.headline: The scripts
scenes.narration: Hiragana is for grammar and native words. Katakana is for loanwords and emphasis. Kanji are characters borrowed from Chinese that carry meaning.
items: Romaji: Latin letters, as a helper

scenes.headline: Not as hard as it sounds
scenes.narration: Hiragana and katakana each have forty-six basic characters, and both are worth learning first.

scenes.headline: Same sound, two scripts
scenes.narration: The word hiragana can be written in hiragana, and katakana in katakana, and they sound the same either way.

scenes.headline: Start with the kana
scenes.narration: Learn a few characters a day and read them aloud.
